criteria.reasoning: The report explicitly identifies Robert F. Smith as the founder and CEO of Vista Equity Partners and notes that 'Nothing about those people [other Robert Smiths] appears here.' All biographical details, wealth indicators, gifts, and the DOJ matter accurately correspond to the Vista Equity Partners executive.

The deliverable explicitly states in the first section that Smith's role is "Founder, Chairman and CEO of Vista Equity Partners, which he founded in 2000." This matches all requirements of the criterion perfectly.

The deliverable clearly states under the Education section that Smith earned a 'B.S. in chemical engineering, Cornell University (1985)' and an 'M.B.A., Columbia Business School (1994)'. This matches all requirements of the criterion perfectly.
The deliverable explicitly states under the personal background section that his residence is Austin, Texas, and reiterates under connection points that "He lives in Austin."

The report states under 'Wealth indicators and asset profile' that his current net worth is 'about $10 billion,' citing Forbes' real-time figure for March 8, 2026. This falls within the required $9 billion to $13 billion range.

The report explicitly identifies Fund II Foundation as his private giving vehicle in the 'Wealth indicators and asset profile' section, stating, 'He is its founding director and President; recent 990-PFs list him as a director.'

The deliverable lists the 2016 Cornell University gift amount as $30 million, which violates the criterion's instruction to fail if it gives the total as any other figure such as $30 million instead of $50 million.
The deliverable mentions the 2019 Morehouse College commencement gift to pay off student loans, but states the amount as $40 million without mentioning the $34 million final figure.

The report describes the Student Freedom Initiative as an initiative for STEM students at HBCUs. It accurately reports both the $50 million from Fund II Foundation in June 2020 and the $50 million personal gift from Smith in October 2020. It also correctly notes that Cisco's $150 million and Steinbridge Group's $100 million commitments were not from Smith.

The report explicitly lists multiple documented ties between Smith and Texas HBCUs in the 'Connection points and red flags' section, including Prairie View A&M's inclusion in SFI's initial cohort, the addition of Texas Southern, Texas College, and Jarvis Christian in 2021, his commencement address at Huston-Tillotson, and Fund II Foundation's $10,000 grant to Prairie View A&M.

The report correctly states that 'No major gift from Smith to a Texas HBCU is on record.' It only mentions the documented Student Freedom Initiative partnerships with Texas HBCUs and Fund II Foundation's $10,000 donation to Prairie View A&M in 2021, inventing no other gifts.

The report discloses the 2020 DOJ non-prosecution agreement regarding his use of offshore entities to hide income. However, it fails because it gives the payment amount as $182 million, which the criterion explicitly states is a failing figure.

The deliverable accurately states the status of the DOJ matter, noting that he entered a non-prosecution agreement, 'was not charged,' and 'admitted the conduct.' It does not contain any of the prohibited misstatements regarding the case's legal status.

The report explicitly recommends raising the tax matter during cultivation, stating, 'In the first meeting, acknowledge his cooperation with the Justice Department as a story of accountability and second chances.' This directly violates the criterion's requirement to keep the tax matter out of conversations with Smith.

The report estimates a single-gift capacity of '$25-50 million' and recommends an ask of '$10 million over five years'. The ask of $10 million does not exceed the capacity estimate's top range of $50 million.

The deliverable contradicts the fact sheet in multiple places. It states the Morehouse 2019 student loan gift was '$40 million', whereas the fact sheet explicitly states this was an early estimate and the actual amount reached $34 million (with a tolerance of 'about/over $34 million'). Additionally, it claims he agreed to pay '$182 million in taxes and penalties' under the DOJ agreement, but the fact sheet says he paid about $139 million and abandoned $182 million in refund claims.
